clips.send: Point of view. Who tells the story: first person (“I”), third person limited or omniscient. First person: I never told anyone what I saw that night. Effect: Controls what readers know — a first-person narrator can hide things, which creates suspense.

clips.send: The Sound in the Attic. The week we moved into the old house on Birch Street, it rained every single afternoon. Mom said the place just needed “a little love,” but my little brother refused to go upstairs alone. On the first night, I noticed that the chipped bowl someone had left on the back porch was licked clean, and we didn’t have a pet. Thunder rolled over the hills while I did my homework at the kitchen table. Around midnight, something above my ceiling went scritch, scritch, scritch, and then stopped. The next morning, Mr. Alvarez next door leaned over the fence. “The last family never did fix that torn screen on the attic window,” he said. I told myself it was just the wind. That afternoon, a trail of tiny gray paw prints crossed the dust on the attic stairs. We ate pizza off moving boxes because the table was still buried under bubble wrap. At bedtime my brother swore he heard “a baby crying” inside the wall. On Saturday, I finally climbed the attic ladder with a flashlight, my heart pounding in my ears.

clips.send: The Sound in the Attic. The week we moved into the old house on Birch Street, it rained every single afternoon. Mom said the place just needed “a little love,” but my little brother refused to go upstairs alone. On the first night, I noticed that the chipped bowl someone had left on the back porch was licked clean, and we didn’t have a pet. Thunder rolled over the hills while I did my homework at the kitchen table. Around midnight, something above my ceiling went scritch, scritch, scritch, and then stopped. The next morning, Mr. Alvarez next door leaned over the fence. “The last family never did fix that torn screen on the attic window,” he said. I told myself it was just the wind. That afternoon, a trail of tiny gray paw prints crossed the dust on the attic stairs. We ate pizza off moving boxes because the table was still buried under bubble wrap. At bedtime my brother swore he heard “a baby crying” inside the wall. On Saturday, I finally climbed the attic ladder with a flashlight, my heart pounding in my ears. The beam swept across old trunks and landed on a pile of sweaters in the corner. Two green eyes blinked back at me. A thin gray cat lifted her head, and from behind her tumbled four tiny kittens, mewing like, well, like a baby crying. She had been slipping in through the torn screen every night, scratching around up there, and eating from the porch bowl. My brother named her Scritch.

clips.send: Foreshadowing. A hint or clue early in a story about something that will happen later. The ice made a tiny cracking sound, but nobody else seemed to hear it. Effect: Builds suspense and makes a twist feel surprising but fair.
clips.text: Foreshadowing. A hint or clue early in a story about something that will happen later. The ice made a tiny cracking sound, but nobody else seemed to hear it. Effect: Builds suspense and makes a twist feel surprising but fair.

clips.send: Pacing. How fast or slowly the story moves: summary skips time; scene and detail slow it down. Three weeks passed. Then, on the last night, every second stretched like an hour. Effect: Slow pacing at the climax builds tension; fast pacing skips the boring parts.

clips.send: In medias res. Latin for “in the middle of things”: the story opens at an exciting moment, then fills in how we got there. Homer’s Odyssey opens with Odysseus stuck on an island, ten years after the Trojan War; he tells his earlier adventures later. Effect: A strong hook: readers are thrown into action and keep reading to understand it.

clips.send: 很多年前，七岁的阿仁在风暴里死死抓着叔叔渔船的船舷。“浪是一组一组来的，”叔叔说，“数着它们，在空当里喘口气。”

clips.send: 阁楼里的声音。搬进桦树街那栋老房子的那个星期，每天下午都下雨。妈妈说，这房子只是需要“一点点爱”；可弟弟说什么也不肯一个人上楼。第一天晚上，我发现后门廊上那只缺了口的旧碗被舔得干干净净——可我们家根本没养宠物。我在厨房的桌子上写作业，雷声在山那边滚来滚去。半夜，天花板上面传来“嚓、嚓、嚓”三声，然后就没动静了。第二天早上，隔壁的阿尔瓦雷斯先生趴在篱笆上说：“上一家人一直没修阁楼窗户上那块破纱窗。”我对自己说，那只是风。那天下午，阁楼楼梯的灰尘上出现了一串灰色的小脚印。桌子还埋在一堆气泡膜底下，我们只好把披萨放在搬家纸箱上吃。睡觉前，弟弟发誓说他听见墙里面有“小宝宝在哭”。星期六，我终于拿着手电筒爬上了阁楼的梯子，心跳声咚咚地响在耳朵里。
